INTRODUCTION

From structure to physiological function

Plant and animal cells share a eukaryotic core, but characteristic plant-cell structures alter photosynthesis, water relations, storage, mechanical support, and cell-to-cell communication. In this lab, use multiple lines of structural evidence rather than relying on a single feature.

Workflow: observe → compare → build → identify → predict/test → explain.

COMPARE

Shared machinery and characteristic differences 10 pts

Treat these as typical comparison patterns, not universal “only in one kingdom” rules.

Structure / featurePlantAnimalPhysiological significance
Nucleus, ER, Golgi, mitochondria, ribosomes, plasma membrane, cytoskeletonPresentPresentShared eukaryotic machinery.
Cellulose-rich cell wallCharacteristicAbsentResists excessive expansion, helps define shape, and contributes to turgor-based support.
Plastids / chloroplastsPresent in appropriate plant tissuesAbsentPhotosynthesis and specialized metabolism.
Dominant central vacuoleCharacteristic of many mature cellsNo equivalent dominant compartmentStorage, ion/pH regulation, turgor, growth, and lytic functions.
PlasmodesmataPresent between many cellsAbsentSymplastic transport and signaling.
Lysosomal degradationLytic vacuoles perform many analogous functionsLysosomes commonIntracellular recycling occurs in both, using differently organized compartments.

MODEL · ASSESSMENT

Build-a-Cell 20 pts

Build both cells by selecting any structure from the organelle bank and then clicking inside either cell. The structure will appear immediately where you place it. All structures remain available for both cells, so decide for yourself which structures belong in each model. Exact organelle position is not graded, except that the nucleolus must be placed inside a nucleus. For the plant cell, the empty outer wall region is shown in a light green; adding a cell wall changes that boundary to a deeper green. Click a placed structure to remove it and reposition it. Use Undo to reverse your last placement or removal. Reset Activity clears all structures from both cells. You have two submission attempts; no right/wrong feedback is given while you work.

IDENTIFY · ASSESSMENT

Classify four unknown cellular specimens 20 pts

For each specimen, choose the most appropriate classification and justify your decision using visible structural evidence. No correctness feedback is provided during the assessment.

PREDICT → TEST → RECORD

Osmosis comparison 20 pts

Complete all six combinations: plant/animal × hypotonic/isotonic/hypertonic. Make your prediction before running each trial. The observed cell image appears only after the simulation is run.
